decision_question: When and under what conditions will Level 4 autonomous driving become commercially viable in major passenger car markets, and what is the addressable market size by 2030?

hypotheses.hypothesis: Level 4 autonomous driving will not achieve widespread consumer adoption in passenger cars before 2030 due to unresolved edge cases and regulatory hurdles.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: If true, investment should focus on commercial fleets and geofenced services rather than consumer vehicles.
needed_evidence: Data on current disengagement rates, regulatory approvals for driverless operations, and consumer surveys on trust.
search_queries: California DMV autonomous vehicle disengagement data

hypotheses.hypothesis: Robotaxi services will achieve profitability in dense urban areas by 2027, driven by lower per-mile costs compared to human-driven ride-hailing.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: If true, robotaxi operators will capture significant market share from Uber/Lyft.
needed_evidence: Cost per mile data for robotaxis vs human drivers, utilization rates, and pricing strategies.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Regulatory approval for Level 4 autonomous driving will be granted first in China (e.g., Beijing, Shanghai) before the US or EU, due to more favorable government policies.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: If true, China will lead in autonomous deployment and related supply chains.
needed_evidence: Timeline of regulatory approvals in China vs US vs EU, number of autonomous vehicle permits issued.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The total addressable market for Level 4 autonomous vehicles in passenger transport will be less than 5% of new car sales by 2030, primarily limited to robotaxis and premium vehicles.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: If true, mass-market OEMs should delay heavy investment in consumer autonomous features.
needed_evidence: Market forecasts from multiple sources, adoption curves of past advanced technologies (e.g., EVs).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Lidar costs will drop below $500 per unit by 2027, making it economically feasible for mass-market Level 4 systems.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: If true, sensor cost reduction will accelerate adoption; if false, reliance on camera-only solutions (Tesla) may win.
needed_evidence: Lidar pricing trends from suppliers (Luminar, Velodyne, Hesai), teardown reports.
search_queries: Tesla camera vs lidar cost comparison

hypotheses.hypothesis: Insurance premiums for Level 4 autonomous vehicles will be 30-50% lower than human-driven vehicles by 2028, due to fewer accidents.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: If true, lower TCO will drive adoption; if false, insurance costs may offset savings.
needed_evidence: Insurance data from autonomous vehicle pilots, accident rates per mile for autonomous vs human.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Consumer willingness to pay for Level 4 autonomy is less than $5,000 per vehicle, limiting adoption to high-end models.
hypotheses.decision_relevance: If true, autonomous features will remain a premium option, not mass-market.
needed_evidence: Consumer surveys on willingness to pay, conjoint analysis results.
search_queries: Consumer willingness to pay autonomous driving feature

market_sizing_plan.sizing_question: How large is the credible opportunity for Future of Autonomous Driving (Sector: Automotive), and which variables still need validation?

methods.formula: Total Addressable Market (TAM) = Global passenger vehicle sales * % of vehicles with Level 4 capability * average selling price premium
known_limitations: Assumes uniform adoption across regions; may overestimate if adoption is concentrated.

methods.formula: Market Size = Sum over regions (Robotaxi fleet size * revenue per robotaxi + Consumer autonomous vehicle sales * ASP)
variables: Consumer autonomous vehicle sales by region
known_limitations: Requires granular data that may not be publicly available; estimates may be speculative.

methods.formula: Potential adopters = Total population * % urban * % with high income * % willing to use autonomous mobility
known_limitations: Funnel conversion rates are uncertain; willingness may not translate to actual use.

methods.formula: Value pool = (Cost savings from reduced accidents + time savings + fuel efficiency) * number of autonomous miles driven
preferred_sources: Bureau of Labor Statistics value of time
search_queries: cost of car accident per mile
known_limitations: Requires assumptions about utilization and behavioral changes; difficult to measure directly.

market_sizing_plan.evidence_rule: Use public source values when available; keep missing variables as validation tasks.

chart_data_needs.title: Robotaxi Cost per Mile vs Human-Driven Ride-Hailing (2024-2030)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: When will robotaxis become cheaper than human-driven ride-hailing?
preferred_sources: Company filings (Waymo, Cruise, Uber, Lyft annual reports)
Industry benchmarks (Uber cost per mile breakdown)
search_queries: Waymo cost per mile robotaxi 2024 annual report
Cruise cost per mile 2023 SEC filing
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use publicly reported cost per mile from company disclosures or credible analyst estimates. If only two endpoints are available, interpolate using CAGR from company targets and mark intermediate years as estimates.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Demonstrate the economic tipping point for robotaxi adoption.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: The report argues that robotaxis will achieve profitability in dense urban areas by 2027. This exhibit must show the cost trajectory.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Robotaxis are projected to undercut human-driven ride-hailing on cost per mile by 2027, supporting the hypothesis of near-term commercial viability.

chart_data_needs.title: Global Level 4 Autonomous Vehicle Sales Forecast by Region (2025-2030)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: Which region will lead Level 4 autonomous vehicle adoption?
required_metrics: Rest of World Level 4 vehicle sales (units)
comparison_set: China, US, EU, Rest of World
search_queries: autonomous vehicle sales forecast by region 2030 McKinsey
Level 4 autonomous car sales China 2025 forecast
IHS Markit autonomous vehicle penetration rate by region
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use published forecasts from at least two credible sources. If regional breakdowns are not available, use global forecast and apply regional shares from regulatory progress reports.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Quantify the market size and regional distribution to support the claim that China leads.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: The report hypothesizes that China will grant regulatory approval first. This exhibit must show the resulting sales forecast.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: China is expected to account for over 40% of global Level 4 sales by 2030, validating the focus on Chinese markets.

chart_data_needs.title: Lidar Cost Reduction Curve (2015-2030)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: When will lidar become affordable for mass-market Level 4 systems?
preferred_sources: Company earnings calls and investor presentations
search_queries: Luminar lidar cost per unit 2023 earnings call
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use actual historical pricing from teardowns or company disclosures. For future years, use company roadmaps or analyst consensus. Mark projected values as estimates.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Show the cost trajectory of a key sensor to support the hypothesis that lidar costs will drop below $500 by 2027.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: The report argues that lidar cost reduction is critical for adoption. This exhibit must show historical and projected costs.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Lidar costs are on track to fall below $500 per unit by 2027, making Level 4 economically feasible for mass-market vehicles.

chart_data_needs.title: Consumer Willingness to Pay for Level 4 Autonomy
chart_data_needs.executive_question: How much are consumers willing to pay for Level 4 autonomous features?
required_metrics: Percentage of respondents willing to pay at each price point
preferred_sources: McKinsey consumer surveys on autonomous driving
search_queries: consumer willingness to pay autonomous driving feature survey 2024 J.D. Power
McKinsey autonomous driving consumer survey 2023 willingness to pay
Deloitte global automotive consumer study 2024 autonomous features
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use published survey data from reputable firms. If regional breakdowns are not available, use global averages and note limitations.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Support the hypothesis that willingness to pay is less than $5,000, limiting adoption to premium segments.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: The report claims that consumer willingness to pay is low. This exhibit must show survey results.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Most consumers are unwilling to pay more than $5,000 for Level 4 autonomy, confirming that it will remain a premium option.

chart_data_needs.title: Regulatory Approval Timeline for Driverless Operations
chart_data_needs.executive_question: How does regulatory pace differ across regions?
required_metrics: Event: Regulatory milestone (e.g., permit granted, law passed)
preferred_sources: Government announcements (China MIIT, US NHTSA, EU Commission)
Permit databases (California DMV, Beijing autonomous vehicle office)
search_queries: California DMV autonomous vehicle permit timeline
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use only official announcements or credible news reports. Include exact dates when available; otherwise, use month/year.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Illustrate the regulatory fragmentation and China's lead.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: The report argues that regulatory approval will be granted first in China. This exhibit must show key milestones.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: China has already granted permits for driverless robotaxis in multiple cities, while US and EU approvals remain limited, supporting the hypothesis of China's lead.

chart_data_needs.title: Autonomous Vehicle Accident Rate per Mile vs Human Drivers
chart_data_needs.executive_question: Are autonomous vehicles safer than human drivers?
required_metrics: Entity: Waymo, Cruise, Human drivers (US average)
search_queries: Waymo accident rate per mile 2023 safety report
NHTSA human driver accident rate per mile 2022
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use official data from NHTSA and state DMV reports. For autonomous vehicles, use company disclosures. Ensure miles driven are reported consistently.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Support the hypothesis that insurance premiums will be lower due to fewer accidents.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: The report claims that autonomous vehicles have fewer accidents. This exhibit must compare accident rates.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Autonomous vehicles have significantly lower accident rates per mile than human drivers, supporting the case for lower insurance costs.

chart_data_needs.title: Autonomous Driving Startup Funding by Year (2015-2024)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: How has investment in autonomous driving evolved?
required_metrics: Top funded companies (Waymo, Cruise, Aurora, etc.)
search_queries: autonomous vehicle investment by year 2015 2024 PitchBook
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use data from venture capital databases. Include only disclosed funding rounds. If exact figures are not available, use estimates from reputable sources.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Show capital formation and investor conviction in the sector.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: The report needs to validate that significant capital is flowing into autonomous driving. This exhibit must show funding trends.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Funding peaked in 2021 but remains substantial, indicating sustained investor interest despite commercialization delays.
